newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Victoria says S&P upgrade endorses budget.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Victoria says S&P upgrade endorses budget.

text.p: The decision by Standard & Poor's Corp to upgrade the credit rating of the state of Victoria was an endorsement of the state government's budget strategy, state Treasurer Alan Stockdale said on Thursday.
"Today's credit rating uppgrade is an emphatic tick upon the state budget strategy, not just on yesterday's budget but on the strategy that's driving that budget," Stockdale told reporters.
S&P earlier announced the upgrade of Victoria's long term local currency debt rating to AA-plus from AA and affirmed its short term rating at A-1 plus.
Stockdale did not say whether the upgrade would help reduce debt servicing costs but noted the state had already achieved interest savings on borrowings to date.
"The importance of this is locking in the benefits we've gained to date," he said.
The action also put Victoria on track for a AAA credit rating by 2000, Stockdale reiterated.
"It puts us right on the pad to launch for a triple A rating ... before the end of the decade," he said.

The state's annual budget document, tabled in state parliament yesterday, unveiled an underlying budget deficit of A$700,000 for fiscal 1996/97 compared with the A$474 million surplus posted for the previous year.
The backbone of the state government's budget strategy has been utilities privatisations, mainly in the electricity sector, to reduce debt.
Stockdale said the 1996/97 budget remained vulnerable to economic growth rates and any restrictions in Commonwealth government funding.
"Our budget is still vulnerable to shocks like cuts in federal funding and downturn in the economy," he said.
"The need to get taxes down to regenerate the state economy is really critical," he added.
